title: ApexMotion — Supplier Risk Intelligence Platform
tagline: Agentic AI platform that detects Tier-1/2/3 supplier disruptions 7–30 days ahead and turns them into evidence-backed, human-approved actions.
context: Euron Consulting FDE program — client engagement case study (Phase 0 design deliverables)
role: Forward Deployed Engineer — solution architecture & design
status: Design complete (Architecture Blueprint, HLD, LLD, Capacity & Cost Plan)
problem: A global manufacturer (4,500 active suppliers, 65,000 SKUs, 6 plants) learned about supplier disruptions too late — often from a Tier-2 or Tier-3 sub-supplier it had no visibility into. It needed early warning across the supply tiers, impact quantified from its own ERP data (no invented numbers), evidence for every claim, and humans accountable for every action — without replacing its ERP, TMS, WMS or PLM systems.
solution: A signal-to-decision platform on AWS. External intelligence (news, weather, ports, regulatory, financial) and operational events stream through Kafka into an S3 + Iceberg lakehouse, are entity-resolved and linked into a Neptune supply knowledge graph, and are triaged cheaply before any LLM call. Deterministic engines compute exposure, time-phased coverage and scenarios; a bounded LangGraph agent running inside Temporal investigates, corroborates, retrieves contract and quality evidence through hybrid RAG, and writes a cited brief that references engine results by ID. Actions are only drafted; execution in source systems needs a single-use human approval token. All model traffic goes through a central LLM gateway that routes by data classification across Amazon Bedrock, self-hosted vLLM/TEI on EKS GPUs and an optional on-prem lane.
highlights: Decomposed the platform into 20 components across 5 logical layers (experience, application, intelligence, data & knowledge, ingestion) with C4 context, container and component views.

Designed a 10-node LangGraph investigation (plan → resolve → corroborate → expose → gather evidence → propose → simulate → synthesise) with hard budgets — 40 steps, 60 tool calls, 150k/15k tokens, 180 s — that return PARTIAL instead of looping.
Kept every number out of the LLM: exposure, coverage and scenario engines own all quantities; the agent cites them by calculation ID and a citation verifier rejects unsupported claims.

Defended against prompt injection structurally: untrusted documents are read only by a tool-less 'quarantined reader' model that returns schema-validated facts; tools are allow-listed, Cedar-authorised on behalf of the user, and side effects are limited to drafts.

Specified a typed tool registry (READ / DRAFT / EXECUTE side-effect classes, per-tool schemas, timeouts, retries and rate limits) and a confidence formula combining entity-match, edge-tier, source-reliability, freshness and consistency scores.

Designed hybrid retrieval on OpenSearch (BM25 + k-NN, BGE-M3 embeddings, reranking, clause-level contract chunking, ACL filtering before retrieval) and a Splink entity-resolution pipeline auto-linking only at ≥ 97% precision.
Built the capacity and cost model: 1.1M → 3.5M events/day, ~21.5M input tokens/day, GPU pool sizing (g6e/L40S) and k-NN memory sizing (36 GB FP32 vs 19 GB FP16).

Ran the managed-vs-self-hosted break-even analysis: the self-hosted GPU lane only becomes cheaper above ~145M tokens/day (~6× Year-1 volume), so it is justified by data control, not cost — and can be deferred without redesign.

Designed for failure: Multi-AZ everywhere, warm-standby DR (RTO ≤ 4 h regional), hash-chained audit ledger anchored to S3 Object Lock, and a deterministic mode that keeps alerting running when every LLM lane is down.
impact: Production run cost modelled at USD 15–25k/month (managed LLM lane) with unit economics of ≈ USD 4.49 per supplier monitored per month.
LLM cost per standard investigation estimated at USD 0.30–0.60; per triaged signal ≈ USD 0.004 — achieved by filtering 100k raw items/day down to ~3k LLM triage calls.
Critical alert path designed for signal → notification p95 ≤ 15 min, independent of LLM availability.
Every requirement mapped to components and a verification method (requirements traceability matrix).

title: Project SENTINEL — Fraud Intelligence LLM for a Payments Company
tagline: Train and self-host a domain LLM that scores every card and UPI transaction, returns ALLOW / REVIEW / BLOCK with a plain-language reason, in ≤ 250 ms p99.
context: Euron FDE program — client engagement case study (PayVista Payments, client requirement document)
status: In progress — requirements analysis and solution design
problem: An RBI-authorised payment aggregator (1.8 lakh merchants, 4.2M transactions/day, 2,800 TPS peaks) saw fraud losses rise from 4.1 to 9.8 bps while its 340-rule engine declined 2.3% of transactions — only 1 in 19 of them actual fraud. Reviewers were drowning (22,000 cases/day), support could not explain declines, and PCI DSS / DPDP rules forbid sending transaction data to third-party AI APIs.
solution: Adapt an open-weight 1B–8B model inside the client's own AWS account: continued pre-training on ~135M tokens of investigator notes, chargeback narratives and playbooks; supervised fine-tuning (LoRA / QLoRA) on transactions serialised into a versioned ≤ 1,024-token prompt with a classification head for the fraud probability; DPO on reviewer preference pairs for grounded explanations; then distillation and INT8 / AWQ quantisation for serving on vLLM / TensorRT-LLM / Triton on EKS GPUs. Engineered features (amount-to-average ratio, new device, geo distance, night-time, failed attempts, velocity) are served from Redis with identical code in training and serving. A configurable rules engine maps calibrated probabilities to ALLOW / REVIEW / BLOCK, hard rules override the model, and the service fails open within 300 ms.
highlights: Broke the client requirement document into objectives, MUST/SHOULD requirements and five acceptance gates (offline accuracy, explanation quality, red-team, load test, shadow pilot).
Engagement must beat an XGBoost baseline on PR-AUC by ≥ +0.03 on a time-split holdout — the baseline is built first and kept warm as a fallback.
Feature set of 10 investigator-derived signals (FE-01 – FE-10), computed only from data available before the transaction to avoid leakage and training–serving skew.
Fraud probability comes from a classification head and is calibrated (temperature / isotonic); explanations are constrained to a JSON schema and may cite only input fields.
Data controls: PII redaction audited on 1,000 documents, holdout-window case notes excluded from training, memorisation test, everything inside the client's AWS account (ap-south-1).
LLMOps plan: PSI drift alerts, BLOCK-rate anomaly alerts, monthly LoRA refresh, 7-day shadow before promotion, 5-minute rollback, all checkpoints versioned in MLflow.
impact: Acceptance targets: recall ≥ 85%, precision at BLOCK ≥ 70%, PR-AUC ≥ 0.80, ≥ 90% factually correct explanations, 100% schema-valid JSON.
Production targets: p99 ≤ 250 ms at 2,800 TPS on ≤ 8 L4 / A10G GPUs, ≤ ₹4.00 inference cost per 1,000 transactions, 99.95% uptime.
Business targets for the 3-month pilot: fraud loss 9.8 → ≤ 6.4 bps, false declines 2.3% → ≤ 1.4%, review queue ≤ 12,000 cases/day.
